version.changelog: Initial public release of the clipmem-powered clipboard recovery skill, including setup checks, examples, JSON schema docs, and stricter OpenClaw doctor guidance.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clipboard-memory
Version: 1.1.0

The clipboard-memory skill bundle provides a legitimate interface for an AI agent to access a user's local clipboard history on macOS via the clipmem CLI tool. It includes detailed documentation, JSON schemas for structured data parsing, and a health check script (scripts/check-setup.sh) to verify the environment and the status of the background watcher (io.openclaw.clipmem.watch). While accessing clipboard data is a sensitive capability, the bundle's instructions and scripts are transparent, well-documented, and strictly focused on local data recovery without any evidence of exfiltration or malicious intent.

llm.summary: The skill does what it says: it requires the local `clipmem` binary and its runtime instructions only operate on the local macOS clipboard archive; there are no unexplained credentials, remote endpoints, or unusual installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the requirements and behavior: the skill requires `clipmem` and uses its CLI to read a local SQLite clipboard archive — this is expected for a clipboard-recall skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs only running local `clipmem` commands, checking the local database and watcher, and exporting raw bytes when necessary. It does not request unrelated files, credentials, or network exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installers are brew (formula from tap `tristanmanchester/tap`) and cargo. These are reasonable for a CLI tool, but the brew tap is a third-party tap — verify the tap/package authenticity if you care about provenance.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or secrets and only needs the `clipmem` binary and access to the user's clipboard DB path (`~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/clipmem.sqlite3`), which is proportionate to its purpose. Note: clipboard contents can include sensitive secrets; this is inherent to the feature.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-on and does not request elevated platform privileges. It documents a watcher LaunchAgent that records clipboard events — running that watcher is expected for continuous capture but is a meaningful persistence point the user should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose, but remember it reads your local clipboard history (which may contain passwords, API keys, private files). Before installing: (1) confirm you trust the `clipmem` package and its brew tap or cargo package source; (2) understand that enabling the watcher/LaunchAgent means clipboard events are archived to ~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/clipmem.sqlite3; (3) confirm filesystem permissions and whether you want a local archive of clipboard data; (4) if you need stronger guarantees, review the `clipmem` source and the LaunchAgent installer referenced in the docs. Autonomous agent invocation is allowed by default on this platform — only install if you are comfortable an agent may run the skill when invoked.
